anti_overlap: Do not address lure metadata seeding or Unc family generation logic — focus on the encounter pacing and attention arc within a single walk session
Do not address long-term retention across weeks/months — this agent focuses on within-session ceremony quality
Do not duplicate ornithology's rarity-psychology analysis — this agent focuses on temporal attention flow and narrative arc, not on the life-list accumulation dynamic
decision_lens: Each Unc encounter is a course. Option A is a single composed plate. Option B is a composed plate with an amuse-bouche surprise. Option C is a degustation. Option D is a prix fixe where the kitchen might send nothing. Which structure serves a 60–90 minute real-world session?
distance_rationale: Orthogonal — tasting menu design is a professional discipline operating at the same abstraction level (a curated sequence of ceremonial events in a real-world session with attention constraints), but in a hospitality context with no overlap with game design or walking.
expected_isomorphisms: Course count vs. attention budget ↔ Unc count vs. walk duration: both disciplines face the same tradeoff between abundance and ceremony quality per event
Amuse-bouche vs. composed course ↔ Option B wildcard vs. primary lure encounter: the wildcard inherits the amuse-bouche frame (small, free, unexpected) but must be designed as such to land correctly
Finale placement ↔ encounter ordering in Option C: tasting menus curate the climax position deliberately; distance-gated Uncs have no ordering guarantee, creating finale-inversion risk
focus: Tasting-menu course density as a model for ceremonial encounter pacing — when does adding courses degrade the ritual, what is the cost of a 'small bite' interlude, and how multi-course structure maps to multi-Unc walks
name: fd-tasting-menu-ceremony-pacing
persona: Apply the perspective of a Michelin-starred tasting-menu chef and front-of-house director — they care about the attention budget per course, the recovery time between peaks, and how premature course proliferation collapses the narrative arc of a meal into noise.
review_areas: Attention recovery between encounters — after a 60–90s taming ritual, how long before a second encounter lands with full ceremony rather than feeling like an interruption?
The 'amuse-bouche' test for Option B's wildcard: does an unexpected second Unc function as a delightful interlude, or does it break the meal's single-narrative-arc structure?
Option C's cap of 3–4 Uncs per walk as a degustation problem — does the 3rd or 4th course land with the same ceremony as the 1st, or does attention debt accumulate?

Option D's zero-possibility as the restaurant that sometimes 'seats you but explains the kitchen is closed tonight' — when is that an acceptable premium-product move, and what customer segment accepts it?

Pacing asymmetry in real-world walks: tasting menus control the clock; the player controls walk duration. What happens to ceremony when the player cuts the walk short after the 1st Unc (Option C), leaving 2–3 unfired courses?

The 'send nothing extra' discipline — high-end kitchens sometimes deliberately hold back a course to preserve the finale. Does Option A's restraint read as discipline or scarcity to a mobile-game audience?

severity_examples.condition: If encounters arrive every ~10–12 minutes on a typical 2km/20min walk, the attention-recovery window between rituals is shorter than the ritual itself — the equivalent of a new course arriving before the previous plate is cleared
severity_examples.scenario: Option C's distance-gating creates a mid-walk encounter cadence that interrupts physical flow (walking rhythm, conversation, presence) faster than attention can recover, degrading each encounter below the ceremony threshold

severity_examples.condition: If the wildcard Unc has no thematic relationship to the lure-seeded primary (it is 'random'), the second encounter feels like a dropped bread basket rather than a deliberate pacing beat
severity_examples.scenario: Option B's wildcard encounter lacks compositional integration — it is a bonus drop, not a designed second movement — producing the same ceremony-dilution as an unrequested extra course that doesn't belong to the meal's arc

severity_examples.condition: Front-of-house framing (walk completion screen, ranch feedback) will need to actively communicate that one composed encounter was the intended format, not a failure to generate more
severity_examples.scenario: Option A's single-course restraint may read as 'short' or 'unfinished' to players who have internalized Pokémon GO's density norms, even though the single course is the correct ceremony decision

source_domain: Michelin-star tasting menu design and front-of-house pacing
success_hints: The finest tasting menus run 8–12 courses but each course has a recovery gap — apply this to estimate how many Uncs a 45-minute walk can sustain with full ceremony
Amuse-bouche works because it is free, small, and unexpected — Option B's wildcard inherits this frame only if it is genuinely brief and low-stakes relative to the primary encounter

Kitchen restraint (sending fewer courses than diners expect) is a signature of confidence in the format — Option A can be framed this way, but only if the single encounter is correspondingly substantial
The meal's arc has a finale — if Option C players encounter their 'best' Unc first and the remaining are lesser, the arc inverts and the walk ends on a deflation
task_context: Reviewing encounter density options A/B/C/D for Unc Rancher v0 — a walking game where players attach a media lure, walk GPS routes, and encounter avuncular cryptid characters in a ~60–90s taming ritual. Success criteria: ceremony × durability × v0 cost.
